121,741 sales worth AED 376 bn were registered from 01 Jan 2026 to 30 Sep 2026. Activity cooled: September had 11,038 sales, 36% fewer than January (partly seasonal — Ramadan, Eid and summer; DLD's open data has no earlier years to compare).
Off-plan dominates: 75% of home sales were off-plan (74% in January, 72% in September); off-plan apartments cost 26% more per sq ft than ready ones.

Like-for-like prices eased: a fixed basket of 47 apartment areas went down 2.3% per sq ft from January to September. They peaked in April (+4.1% vs January) and eased after. The simple city average went down 12.4%, but 10.1 points of that come from more sales in cheaper areas (a mix effect), not from prices.

Demand is concentrated in affordable areas: Madinat Al Mataar, Jumeirah Village Circle and Dubai Land Residence Complex take 24% of apartment sales, and 10 of the 15 busiest areas sell below the city median of AED 1,714 per sq ft.
Mid-market buyers: 68% of homes sold for under AED 2M and 71% of apartments were studios or 1-bedrooms.

Cheaper areas pay back faster: the cheapest third of 35 areas earns a median 8.3% gross rental yield vs 5.4% for the priciest third. Top: Dubai Investment Park Second (9.7%), Dubai Land Residence Complex (9.3%), Dubai Production City (9.3%); lowest: Palm Jumeirah (4.7%).
